counterfactual_missing_items: Classic upper-body SVC obstructive signs such as face/upper extremity edema or neck vein distention are not explicitly reported
No histologic/pathologic confirmation establishes that the obstructing fat mass is a true cardiac lipoma rather than another fat-containing lesion
The vignette does not state whether fat-suppressed MRI sequences or biopsy were used to formally confirm lipoma tissue subtype
decisive_items: SVC peak flow velocity: 74 cm/s cephalad to mass, 124 cm/s caudal to mass
MRA showed narrowing of the SVC and decreased blood flow through the site of compression
3.1 × 2.3 × 3.0 cm well-defined mass within the lower SVC with extension to the interatrial septum
response.rationale: R1 directly ties the patient’s exertional dyspnea and exercise-induced blood pressure fall to objectively demonstrated SVC narrowing, accelerated caudal flow velocity, and MRI/MRA compression. R2 explains only the fat-containing mass appearance and does not integrate the hemodynamic SVC obstruction syndrome. R1 is therefore more complete clinically and imagingwise, with R2 as a supportive tissue-level differential.

rejected.why: It is supported only by the fat-signal mass appearance and does not explain or account for the SVC velocity gradient, MRA narrowing/decreased flow, exertional symptoms, or blood-pressure drops indicative of active SVC obstruction.
